candidates.problem: For $a=1/2$, the left-hand side of the cited formula is $\pi\cot(\pi/2)=0$. The telescoping sum is part of the right-hand side and equals $2$; hence the right-hand side is $1/a-2a\cdot 2=2-2=0$, not $2-0=2$. The passage also mislabels the telescoping series as the left-hand side.
candidates.proposed_fix: For $a=1/2$, the right-hand side should be $2-2=0$ and the left-hand side is $0$; the telescoping sum is a term in the right-hand side and equals $2$.

candidates.title: The statement does not exclude \(a=0\). If \(a=0\), the condition only fixes \(0
candidates.quote: $a\in\mathbb{D}$ について、$0$ と $a$ を入れ替える $\mathbb{D}$ の自己同型を求めよ。それは対合（2 回合成すると恒等写像）か。
candidates.problem: The statement does not exclude \(a=0\). If \(a=0\), the condition only fixes \(0\), so there is no unique automorphism; all rotations \(z\mapsto cz\) with \(|c|=1\) fix \(0\), but such rotations need not be involutions. Thus “the” automorphism and whether “it” is an involution are not well-defined.
candidates.proposed_fix: Require \(a\ne 0\), or treat \(a=0\) separately. For \(a\in\mathbb{D}\setminus\{0\}\), there is a unique disk automorphism exchanging \(0\) and \(a\), and it is involutive. For \(a=0\), every rotation \(z\mapsto cz\), \(|c|=1\), fixes \(0\), and among these only \(c=\pm1\) give involutions.
